test_title: PYST 26: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 20th Sep 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The spokesperson claimed yesterday (1)/ that all disputes have been settled (2)/ although no supporting documents (3)/ were released publicly. (4)/
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the usage of the present perfect tense "have been" in part 2.
 
• Since the statement refers to an event that occurred in the past (yesterday), the past perfect tense "had been" should be used.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The spokesperson claimed yesterday that all disputes **had been** settled although no supporting documents were released publicly."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The spokesperson claimed yesterday" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "although no supporting documents" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **4: "were released publicly." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
